The south ridge is a rated 4th-class, exposed scramble to a 3,048 m summit on the Alberta/BC divide, and the FKT track file is the south-ridge line from the Interlakes area.

area.name: Mount Northover
area.blurb: Mount Northover is a 3,048 m summit on the Continental Divide on the Alberta and British Columbia border, standing at the head of the Three Isle, Aster and Joffre creek valleys in the Kananaskis backcountry. It is a serious scrambler's peak, usually reached from camps at Aster or Three Isle lakes.

route.name: South Ridge
route.rock_grade: Exposed 4th class on a narrow ridge with a harder chimney-like crack below the top
route.best_season: Dry, snow-free late summer. Snow or ice on the ridge makes it far more dangerous.
route.overview: The South Ridge is the usual way up Mount Northover, a 3,048 m peak on the Continental Divide in the Kananaskis backcountry. Easy grass and slab lead onto a narrow, exposed ridge with cliff bands and loose rubble, and a steep summit block finishes the climb. It is a serious, committing scramble with real fall consequences.
route.beta: From the Aster Lake flats, head up grassy lower slopes and easy slabs to the start of the ridge. The crest narrows with big drops on both sides, broken by cliff bands and loose rubble. Near the top the angle steepens at the summit block; the hardest moves are a chimney-like crack just below the top, which can be avoided by a ledge traverse to a crack that leads to the summit. Terrain just off the line is harder than the route, so staying on it matters.
route.descent_text: Many parties come down the same ridge. An alternative descent goes west from the south summit over steep, loose, exposed ground to a col and shoulder, then back toward Aster Lake; it is loose 4th class.
hazards: Severe exposure on the narrow ridge
Loose rock on the ascent and descent
Fatigue and route-finding errors late in the day
Snow and ice make the route much more dangerous

area.name: Ossa Mountain
area.blurb: Ossa Mountain is a 2,261 m summit in the Tantalus Range northwest of Squamish, with views across the Sunshine Coast ranges and Mount Tantalus. It is the more reachable of the Tantalus peaks, with a scramble as its easiest route.

route.name: East Ridge
route.rock_grade: Class 4 scrambling with a downclimb into a notch and a chimney crux near the top
route.best_season: Midsummer to early fall, once snow has melted off the upper mountain; any glacier cover on the trail calls for crampons and an axe.
route.overview: Ossa Mountain is climbed by its east ridge, a long day from the Squamish side with steep forest, meadows and creek crossings below a route-finding scramble. Near the top the route downclimbs into a notch and works through a chimney section before the summit.
route.beta: Climb steeply through forest and meadows, crossing creeks, to the upper mountain. The upper scramble is hard to follow: expect route-finding, a downclimb into a notch, and a crux in chimneys. Plenty of water is available lower down.
route.descent_text: Return the same way; the downclimbs and loose ground make the descent as serious as the ascent.
hazards: Snow or glacier cover early in the season
gear: Ice axe and crampons if snow or ice remains

approach_logistics.trailhead: Ossa Mountain trailhead, about 30 minutes from Squamish

area.name: South Pioneer Peak
area.blurb: South Pioneer Peak is the trail-accessible southern summit of Pioneer Peak, the Chugach landmark standing over the Knik River valley south of Palmer. A relentless ridge trail climbs from near sea level to a saddle, and a rough scramble leads to the top.

route.name: Pioneer Ridge
route.rock_grade: Off-and-on Class 3 scrambling on the summit ridge
route.best_season: Summer, once snow has melted off the saddle and ridge; patches can linger into late June.
route.overview: The Pioneer Ridge route climbs about 6,000 feet in one push from the Knik River valley, through forest and brush onto open tundra ridge and then to a saddle near 5,200 ft. A rough, exposed scramble along the ridge reaches the south summit.
route.beta: Follow the steep trail through forest and alder to treeline, then up tundra and switchbacks to the saddle near 5,200 ft. From there the route heads northeast along the ridge, rolling at first and steepening, with off-and-on Class 3 scrambling near the top. Keep to the east side of the ridge after the false summit.
route.descent_text: Descend the same way, with extra care on the loose, exposed ridge, then the long trail back to the car.
hazards: Exposure and loose rock on the ridge
Sparse water above the lower trail
Heat and insects in the forest
Devil's club and thick brush on the lower trail

approach_logistics.trailhead: Pioneer Ridge Trailhead, Knik River Road

area.name: Mount Olomana
area.blurb: Mount Olomana is a sharp three-summit ridge on the windward side of Oahu, between Kailua and Waimanalo, a remnant of the old Koolau volcano. Locals compare it to a miniature Matterhorn for its steep, narrow profile.

route.name: North Ridge (First Peak)
route.rock_grade: Class 3 scrambling with a roughly 15 ft Class 4 step near the first summit
route.best_season: Dry, calm days; avoid the trail during or just after rain, when the dirt turns very slippery.
route.overview: The North Ridge route climbs through rainforest and red dirt to the first summit of Olomana, the highest of its three peaks. A steep final boulder step is usually protected by unofficial fixed ropes of unknown condition. The second and third peaks are far more exposed and are not part of this route.
route.beta: Walk the paved country-club road to the signed trail, then follow a nearly flat track through rainforest past an abandoned water station. At an exposed red-dirt junction, climb the ridge through ironwood trees. Near the top there is Class 3 scrambling and a roughly 15 ft Class 4 section, often aided by old fixed ropes, then some exposed scrambling to the summit.
route.descent_text: Return the same way, down-climbing the steep boulder step with care; descending the exposed sections is harder than climbing them.
hazards: Fixed ropes are unofficial and of unknown condition
Drop-offs on one or both sides of the ridge
Slippery dirt and rock when wet

approach_logistics.trailhead: Olomana trailhead, off the golf-club road, Maunawili
